question: with the FINAL band (full_family, 2 sigma = 0.049752 ns), does the gate-level graph-feature signal survive? and is it a CANDIDATE-level signal a generator can use, or a POOL-level one it cannot?

control_faithfulness.note: the control pass runs at the band in force and reproduces the artefacts the finalisation chain just wrote -- so these numbers are the finalised ones, not a re-derivation

verdicts.the_preview_held: the LOG-23 preview predicted the final band to within 1.3% and every qualitative conclusion held: the graph features stay at/below random on resolvable and harm, the gain label stays the one exception, the cheap placed stage stays the strongest single feature, and the acceptance criterion keeps its physical selectivity with a STRONGER harm ratio
verdicts.candidate_level_verdict: on the reading a candidate generator can use -- within one pool -- every graph feature set is level with the trivial kind-only baseline in BOTH families and on ALL THREE labels; the apparently large pooled numbers are reproduced by a predictor that only knows the pool mean, so they are between-pool effects
verdicts.magnitude_not_topology: the features that do carry signal (depth, max_fanout) predict harm as strongly as they predict resolvable, i.e. they predict how FAR the WNS moves, not WHICH WAY
verdicts.what_it_means_for_the_gnn_idea: in this family, with scalar summaries of the gate-level graph, there is no candidate-level information a GNN could exploit beyond the candidate kind and the iteration; the usable levers are the cheap placed-stage label and a pool-level prior (some pools are worth measuring first)

boundaries: post-hoc: the split sets and the single features were chosen by looking at the data (9-11 sets x 3 labels x 2 families); no nested selection was run, so the CIs are not multiplicity-corrected.
the graph features are scalar summaries of the gate-level graph, NOT a GNN encoder -- "no signal in the summaries" does not prove "no signal in a GNN".
the pooled reading mixes a strong between-circuit component (per-circuit positive rate 0.207-0.616 on ITC-99); the within-pool reading is the one a candidate generator can use.

the parasitics come from estimate_parasitics, not from a signoff RC extraction; the placed and routed tiers use different estimation models, so "routed - placed" mixes a stage change with a model change.
